verdict.tagline: Rough server connections and shaky cutscenes mar an otherwise engaging shooter.
for_you_if: you want an aggressive co-op shooter
you plan to push past the rough opening
you enjoy testing complex combat builds
not_for_you_if: you need reliable offline single-player access
you want working map and quest navigation
you expect smooth performance without crashes

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the menus and user interface as slow, clunky, and heavily resembling Destiny.

citations.review_text:
This game brought me back to when I played Destiny 1 for the first time, Such a riot. 
Only an hour in so far and this game is like a love child between Gears of War & Destiny. It's great. The powers add depth that break up the TPS gameplay in a familiar way that destiny does, and the cover shooting and bulky character bodies are very similar to Gears of War and bullet storm. Sadly, the character customization is pretty limited and the menus and UI are a copy of destiny :/ The story is also pretty generic and heavy handed, but not awful just meh. If you choose to go through the prologue it can be overbearing, however you are free to skip any scene. You also get dialogue options for your character, but I don't believe any of the options affect things much, at least not at the start. However, the gameplay is really where this game shines and with the added difficulty options for better loot drops, I can already see myself playing this one often

I tried this game at release and it was pretty bad, so I decided to refund and let it cook for a while.
For a game that's been out for 3 years now it's absolute garbage.
The menu's are slow and clunky and sometimes even unresponsive.
This game will clearly never be good.
I hope Square learned a lesson with this one and stops publishing games made by second-rate developers.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the map system as poorly designed, lacking a north direction and accurate quest pathing.

citations.review_text:
This game is pretty underrated, unfortunately. It's not perfect, but it's very enjoyable and has some features that rival every game I've ever played. The weapon and character skins are probably the best I've ever seen in a videogame - sometimes I come across a new weapon skin and think "man I need to try more games made by this dev (People Can Fly). NPC dialog is not "cheesy", and the story is pretty interesting. The combat can become repetitious when you reach endgame but on your way there you'll need to be methodical and the game provides that approach. Weapons and gear have pretty good perks so building is interesting, and each class has a variety of skills and a pretty nice skill tree - all classes can handle endgame content when built right and all classes can be a lot of fun. The enemies actually look like a threat, great design there as well. It has solo and full cross play co-op campaign...

It has it's flaws - it's a must be online always game, the map somewhat sucks, the amount of cover implemented in most combat areas, though appreciated, takes away from the level design... anyway. I def recommend. Try it out, you'll have fun if this is your genre.

Game is fun but the writing is not great and the map mechanic is one of the worst I've ever seen in a polished game. There is no north direction and no way to identify where you are on the map other than a very broad region. 50% of the time the quest path brings you to the wrong place.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that changing areas involves short loading screens and mini cutscenes between rooms.

citations.review_text:
I cannot recommend this game.
Whoever design the system of Cinematic to then have to teleport back to base and get a loading screen has to be fired. When you finish the mission, teleport me back directly.

I have never seen so many cinematic leading to loading screen to the more cinematic.

You play 2 mins, cinematic.

gameplay is Temu GoW with Destiny 2.
Don't bother.

Heres the thing, I've tried to play this game before, a few years back. The games style, general gameplay loop, and classes are very interesting and cool. And if the rest of the game was as good as them, i would happily recommend this game. But it suffers several problems that make it so i can't recommend it. First and foremost, the constant loading zones and mini cutscenes. The game has to load every single area every single time you go to a new room. Its like playing monster hunter 3 all over again. You can barely walk through a door without needing a tiny cutscene showing you opening the door for 2-3 seconds and then you load into a new area. The areas are not that large, you are only in them for 5 or so minutes at a time before needing to move on to the next. These areas are not so details and or complex that they need to load every single time you go through. The constant black screen, followed by 3-5 second cutscene just to load a room with a handful of enemies that don't even spawn till you reach a trigger is agonizing.
The second thing is you're basically always poor, at least i was. You get basically no money if any from quests and side quests, so if you ever want a new gun. you need to save up and sell everything you find to be able to afford one new gun or piece of armor, because it will cost you everything you have. The game does not reward you enough for doing side quests and the likes because you usually get a single piece of armor or weapon for each side quest, and a lot of the time it isn't even an upgrade so you either sell it or break it down.
Lastly is the leveling pace. For most of my playtime i had the world tiers automatically scale as i unlocked them. What this does is its supposed to make you get more exp, better loot, but enemies are scaled a number of levels above you at all times. For a while that's fine, the increase in difficulty is manageable, but after a while the enemies are so much higher level than you that it makes certain enemie…

After several hours play I can't give this game a recommend. I played co-op with a friend and we didn't have any bugs or issues. All the elements on their own seem fine, you can level up, collect gear, use a variety of weapons and abilities. The levels are linear but there are some good moments in the level design. The primary issue I had was just waiting for all these elements to gel so the game could click. 

The gunplay and abilities just don't feel like they pack the right amount of punch. The enemies all feel very bullet spongy and the best tactics for defeating them seem to lean heavily towards staying in cover and playing it safe. The equipment upgrades are small with you noticing very little difference. Same with the abilities. The game turns into a slog without really ever feeling satisfying. There are some other gripes also. The game appears to have been optimized for playstation as changing areas requires a short 5 second loading cutscene which breaks the flow of the game.

The writing is also terrible. Admitedly we've been spoiled by the amazing writing in some recent titles (E33 comes to mind), but I can forgive most writing as long as it's servicible. The writing in Outrider feels like it's trying to take the macho over the top tone of an 80's action movie but with the cringefest execution of a Joss Whedon film. 

If you want a co-op game with gunplay, RPG mechanics, and abilities I'd strongly recommend you give Outriders a miss and pick up Remnant 2 instead.

claims.claim: Reviewers report technical issues such as audio bugs, enemies getting stuck in walls, and graphical or HDR rendering problems during cutscenes.

citations.review_text:
tl;dr Final rating is a 6/10 for me. Originally no lifed on xbox and recently bought on pc.

So for starters the game is dead which means bugs and stuff which have been present since the last update are still there. I had to make my own .pak mods using UE to fix various audio bugs (like the geiger counter ticking lol) and even some weird UI bugs and class screen bugs (which im sure now im flagged as a cheater for using them but oh well I don't like hearing a dang geiger counter for 4 hours or having to restart my game cause it gives me the wrong class' class point screen lmao). Now that made me rate the game an 8/10, however this next bit made me drop 2 more points off my rating. Sooo this next gripe stems from the forced server connection. I have had over 50 bosses and minibosses combined that just stood there while I shot them during my campaign run due to the forced server connection buggin out... Don't get me wrong the game runs smoothly I maxed all the scalability group settings out, and even tinkered with 20+ renderer settings in via the egnine.ini to achieve a beautiful cinematic look. I am also using ReShade to mimic my monitors HDR, bloom tweaks and curves then stacking Nvidia Filters to fine tune details with sharpening and stuff. The game is looking amazing and I can easily hold a stable 120 fps on my work laptop which is running a Legacy GTX 1650 and 40gb of ram. With all that being said due to the issues that stem from being forced to connect to a server constantly and then having disconnects during boss fights or something else dumb going on I am rating this game a 6/10. I loved it on release and still do but the game is dated and its also dead so keep that in mind when you buy it (I'd recommend only buying it on sale). Also keep in mind that there are currently no plans to give the game an offline port and the game is struggling to keep less than 500 daily players (not all at once like at the time of writing this it is at 178 in game) so the servers…

A mediocre cover looter shooter with an unplayably bad HDR, rendering cutscenes either too bright or too dark and parts of gameplay unbearable (e.g. Eagle Peaks). Don't buy, as the devs abandoned the game in its broken state and won't fix this bug ever.

Played for a bit with a buddy when it first released, but never finished.
Came back to try it solo and there are somehow more issues?

-Enemies have no sounds/gun animations leading to me just taking damage without knowing where/why for a minute. (I turned off V-Sync, Frame limit cap, and swapped to DX11 to no avail). 
-The cover button and/or the cover mechanic just doesn't work sometimes and your character just crouches for a half second before standing back up.
-Had enemies get stuck in walls/outside the map leading to a forced reset on the mission.
-Not a "real" problem, but why is the melee attack 20x louder than everything else?

Not sure what happened, but this was on a fresh install and also after verifying integrity as well. Tried every fix I could find off old subreddits and YT videos, but problems kept reappearing.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game requires an internet connection to play.

citations.review_text:
Let’s be honest: mechanically, this game is decent. The movement has some weight to it and the TFP combat is serviceable, especially if you enjoy Gears-style cover shooting mixed with supernatural abilities. But it's nowhere near as satisfying or polished as the games it clearly draws inspiration from.
But the execution? A complete masterclass in how to ruin a decent game with corporate brain-damage.
First off: Forced "Always-Online" for a pure solo campaign. Who in their right mind thought it was a genius engineering decision to chain a single-player story to a live server queue? If you are playing on a shared connection, a repeater, or a mobile hotspot, this game is completely unplayable.
Second: The PC optimization is absolute garbage. Beautifully optimized masterpieces like Gears 5 run flawlessly on High settings on older Pascal architecture like a GTX 1060. Outriders? It chugs along at a cinematic, unplayable 15 FPS slideshow during basic combat encounters. 
The developers completely shot themselves in the foot. They built a heavy-hitting, grounded sci-fi shooter and then locked it behind terrible engine code and an anti-cheat server firewall that actively punishes legal, paying solo players.
Do not buy this full price, and honestly, think twice even if it's on a deep discount. Total garbage infrastructure.

This game is pretty underrated, unfortunately. It's not perfect, but it's very enjoyable and has some features that rival every game I've ever played. The weapon and character skins are probably the best I've ever seen in a videogame - sometimes I come across a new weapon skin and think "man I need to try more games made by this dev (People Can Fly). NPC dialog is not "cheesy", and the story is pretty interesting. The combat can become repetitious when you reach endgame but on your way there you'll need to be methodical and the game provides that approach. Weapons and gear have pretty good perks so building is interesting, and each class has a variety of skills and a pretty nice skill tree - all classes can handle endgame content when built right and all classes can be a lot of fun. The enemies actually look like a threat, great design there as well. It has solo and full cross play co-op campaign...

It has it's flaws - it's a must be online always game, the map somewhat sucks, the amount of cover implemented in most combat areas, though appreciated, takes away from the level design... anyway. I def recommend. Try it out, you'll have fun if this is your genre.

Im having a really great time with this game. Great gameplay + great voice acting, + good story, + good sidequests, etc. Only thing that stuck out as a problem was the "always online" feature, but i only got one DC up to now (about 15 hours in)

Overall id recommend it! If youre a fan of looter shooters you will have fun with this one

yep, exactly what most neg reviews say, got this on sale and the stupid thing is'nt supported by the devs and still requires a presistant internet connection to play. Just got disconnected for the umpteenth time and well...not a reccomendation. Other than that, the game is nothing special. Not recommended.

My oh my, how gaming on a budget has become mainstream for those not wanting to rain $60, $70 and $80 on publishers or hundreds, thousands on greedy hardware companies that care little for the little guy / gal when they get in bed with monstrous A.I. conglomerates. citations.review_text:
You've heard of "Bulletstorm", now meet "Bulletsponge".

This game is dead, with barely 29 people active at all time. Quest markers are wonky, and in some sections fast travel doesn't even work.

It's a shame, because it could be a casual shooter to pass the time with, instead, I feel like I'm frantically running around at all times with this game...

I purchased this game on a discount looking for a fun third person shooter. And that's what I got. What I didn't expect is to also find a good and engaging story in a game like this. I would 100% recommend this game. 

As pros: The combat is fun, the looting aspect is good as well. The progression is fun and engaging. Playing on the highest world tier, as long as your build makes some sense, is not very difficult. You get pretty overpowered by the end. The story as I said is interesting and worth doing, and the sidequests are not endless, you get like 1-3 per zone, and are worth doing as it adds to the mainstory. 

Cons: There is some jank, but not enough to take away from what's good. I got a bug where the quest tracker pointed to the wrong quest, after i finished one. Relogging fixed that so it's not that big of a deal. Gameplay is pretty much the same from the first zone to the last one. What keeps it fresh is the loot, build, and actually good variety of places you visit. 

There is also an endgame, that i didn't dive into yet. I want to get the DLC and get into that as well. But for now I'm satisfied with the campaign. 

No brainer on a discount if you want some fun third person shooting. Imo it's worth full price, but i got it on discount so that's up to you. This is a much better game than i expected it to be.

A great storyline, good voice acting, good looking graphics, lots of enemy types and plenty of variety when it comes to locations.
And then there's endgame content. Expeditions (like dungeons) give you materials (to upgrade gear) and legendary weapon. Though it can be a bit grindy but I still like it.

Some bugs, like map quest markers not working sometimes or showing the wrong direction, but overall it's pretty bug-free.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the in-game cover mechanic is useless because aggressive enemies flush players out and flank them.

citations.review_text:
I have put dozens of hours into this game and up until this exact moment, I still don't know if I actually like it.

I love looter shooters. I’ve put obscene amounts of time into the Borderlands series, so I thought I knew what I was getting into. Outriders is not that. It is completely unpolished. The graphics are noticeably janky, the cutscene camera shakes like the cameraman is actively running for his life, and the game tricks you into thinking it has a cover mechanic. Word of advice: The cover is completely useless. If you try to play this like a tactical shooter, the aggressive AI will flush you out, flank you, and absolutely turn you to ash in four seconds.

The gameplay loop is pure, unadulterated chaos. You heal by killing, so you are forced to run face-first into gunfire like a lunatic, spamming sci-fi space magic just to stay alive. It’s stressful, ugly, and frantic.

But the one thing keeping me from uninstalling is the brilliant crafting system. Being able to break down weapons and gear to permanently strip their mods into a universal library is genius. It makes every piece of trash loot feel useful because you can just slap a ridiculous tier-3 lightning strike mod onto a standard shotgun later.

It is rough around the edges, lacks that smooth Borderlands polish, and will occasionally infuriate you. But when the space magic clicks and the screen explodes in numbers, it’s a weirdly good time. Proceed with caution.

Though recommended requirements state: Intel i7-7700K / AMD Ryzen 5 2600X for a 1080P / 60 FPS experience I'm playing this on a 2009 I7-920 @1080P / 60 FPS.  Admittedly I'm using Lossless Scaling which most think of as a GPU utility though can significantly reduce CPU load as well.   

I acquired the game through a Humble Bundle 1st tier @$10 and given the four really good games in that tier, my mathematical enriched brain calculates my Outriders purchase to a whooping $2.50.  My oh my, how gaming on a budget has become mainstream for those not wanting to rain $60, $70 and $80 on publishers or hundreds, thousands on greedy hardware companies that care little for the little guy / gal when they get in bed with monstrous A.I. conglomerates.  I'm of course speaking of ridiculous RAM prices.

Are you Not Entertained?  Isn't that why you are here?

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0gmKQ8oqoF4

As for the game.  The crowd here has significantly dwindled and the curtains may soon close unable to be resurrected by the removal of an always online requirement. 

The game is good.  Outriders serves it's solo player well.  I love the numerous skills and the cover and shoot combat is serviceable though there is a class where you will not be using cover much and it rocks.  There are something like 16 difficulty tiers... amazing.  I've not seen that many tiers since Hilary lost to Donald (get it tiers / tears lol).  Personally I think the story and the lore has been exceptional but of course my opinion is subjective.

Who knows how long the servers will be up.  Hilary could wipe them any day </snicker>.  Seriously though not many playing and unless you have a friend you're most likely to go solo.  Be an Outrider!  You'll be very enamored with yourself.  Be entertained!

Yes, would recommend it, glad my friends and I bought it in the sale.
Bad bits: Mapping. I am talking about side quest mapping here - the markers are not necessarily where they seem to be on the main map. The map marker will often point you directly back to where you have just come from, had to leave the game and come back in to get the entrances to work at times.
Not being able to place your own waypoint is annoying, you can only see where you are at a camp or flag, as in, can't see if you are going the right way.
Mods - not being able to replace both mods on weapons or armor

Good bits: Was not expecting any story whatsoever, am impressed with the depth and breadth of this one. Dark and gritty with squalid townships that add to the ambience - have been and still am interested enough to keep going.
Gear drops are plentiful from fighting.
Rewards are fairly good for completing tasks/side quests.
Shopkeepers have some fairly good stuff BUT it's very expensive, you need to be sure you really want that gun/armor piece - I am at only mebbe level 22? and most of their stuff even in their daily sale is around 20K - out of the current 40k I have....you see what I mean.
Game runs well on my rig - had only one instance of being stuck in a co-op game at a store. Having to come out to make the buggy map marker fix itself is the only other issue I've had.
Combat is fun as are the powers.
*later edit* - bought the dlc and really enjoyed it - overall, this game is underrated. Yes, there are some bugs at times but it's beautifully built. Funny, sad, poignant and an interesting commentary on the state of humanity. My friends and I are really pleased we got it - it's very very good.
I love this game, the builds were so fun, In the end I platinumed it on PS5.  Only thing that stood out about hating it was the broken waypoint marker.  But yeah, coop or alone, this game was so fun.

Such a fun game! Co-op can be tough sometimes, particularly early on, but solo is even more challenging early on. Either way though, the game is a blast! Great skill options, with lots of crafting to keep your gear upgraded if you up the levels as you progress. There is the option to not increase levels, but the challenge of higher and higher difficulty (with upgraded gear) is too much fun to pass up.

A great storyline, good voice acting, good looking graphics, lots of enemy types and plenty of variety when it comes to locations. Worldslayer DLC is the icing on the cake, adding to the story with more fun gameplay and locations. Tarya Gratar location is quite challenging with lots of varying bosses, but the rewards are great and plentiful. In fact, rewards are very plentiful all throughout the entire game and DLC.

And then there's endgame content. Expeditions (like dungeons) give you materials (to upgrade gear) and upgraded gear. Though it can be a bit grindy to get the mats needed as you level up, I still like it.

Some bugs, like map quest markers not working  sometimes or showing the wrong direction, but overall it's pretty bug-free. The biggest con for the game is that it's an online service, even in solo play - which really sux if Steam goes down or your internet is offline!!

I would LOVE to see and Outriders 2, but I'm doubtful it would happen since this game had a bit of a rocky start. In it's current state though, the game is a lot of fun!

Highly recommend if you don't mind crafting and a bit of grind sometimes.

Truly is a good game. Had a rocky start, with server issues along with being online-only. But it 100% is worth playing.

The gunplay feels real good; it's a true looter shooter where 90% of your strength comes from items. Decent build variety. It even has a decent story. A solid 8/10.

The good: Excellent combat and classes. Great gear customization and progression. Most everything in the game looks and sounds wonderful. Everything in the game can be done solo if needed. Many enemies actually offer a challenge until learning and unlocking various things.

The mid: The story. This game is a story/campaign game and it's not a long ride. Most zones are designed with the same structure/formula.

The bad: Sparce and repetitive end game. There are no dedicated sources for items and getting a desired item with a desired mod is going to be a fraction of 1% chance each attempt. Even when playing single player, this is another game that requires online play. The game is still prone to occasional disconnects that can reset your progress in long fights and endgame areas. Sniper rifles are awful.

Biggest highlight for me: Being able to use a class skill to leap long distances, through walls, and crash land onto globs of snipers before wiping them out with a shotgun that procs fiery explosions. Just awesome gameplay.

7.5/10 - If pigs fly and they make an Outriders 2, check it out because this game was very close to being amazing.
